newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia wildcat lumber strike ends.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia wildcat lumber strike ends.

text.p: Wildcat strikes at International Forest Products Ltd ended late on Friday, paving the way for a restart of labor negotiations for British Columbia's lumber industry.
Mike Wilson, sawmill supervisor at Interfor's McDonald cedar mill, said the company served the strikers with cease and desist orders at about 2000 EDT/2400 GMT Friday evening.

"The information pickets are coming down as we speak," Wilson said. He said workers could be back on the job in some mills as early as Friday night, while others plants would restart operations over the weekend.

The wildcat strikes by about 1,600 Interfor workers broke out at the company's facilities in the lower mainland of British Columbia Friday morning after Interfor announced plans to close the McDonald sawmill.

The job action prompted Forest Industrial Relations, which bargains on behalf of 65 forest companies, to cancel negotiations with the Canadian lumber workers' union, IWA-Canada. The two sides have been bargaining for a new labor contract for the coastal lumber industry.
FIR's chief negotiator Keith Bennett said the end of the wildcat strike bodes well for the early resumption of talks.
"If the mills are all running normally over the weekend, I would expect we could get started early next week," Bennett told Reuters.

Sources have negotiations could resume on Tuesday, but there were no meetings scheduled yet. Despite a disagreement between the two sides over wages, officials have said a contract deal was within reach.
